title: Stylists versus players: Hawkins, Young, Miles and Dizzy
summary: Sam separates stylists like Lester Young and Miles from fine players like Chu Berry and Dizzy.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Yeah because they have a different style of playing and what he does, he does well, you know. He have a following in each of their field. Like Lester Young, he had a following. Coleman Hawkins had a following and they both was fantastic saxophone players. They both were stylists.
Then you had Ben Webster around then. You had Chu Berry. A whole bunch of band cats, you know.

All those people. Yeah but see now although that you had Ben Webster and Chu Berry but Coleman Hawkins and Lester Young were stylists, you see. Therefore they were more popular than Ben Webster and Chu Berry, you see.

Okay Lester Young played less notes. Coleman Hawkins played a lot of notes. But he still was a stylist because when he played a melody, he could be just as interested in playing a melody and improvising it through as Lester Young. Lester Young played less notes but he made a melody make sense, you see, more interesting. Where if Chu Berry played it, he couldn't play it as good, made sense as good as Coleman Hawkins or Lester Young. But he is also a fantastic saxophone player.
There is a difference between a stylist and a regular player, you see. It's like Miles Davis is a stylist and Dizzy Gillespie is a player, you see.

Miles plays less notes. Dizzy plays a lot of notes, you see. So that's the way it's different between and so the people they compared, they never thought and sat down and said what you say. These guys, it's fantastic, both of them so how can you compare them. Because they both is giants you know.
